About Me

Serving the farmers and animals of Baliakandi

I am a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine currently serving as the Upazila Livestock Officer of Baliakandi, Rajbari, under the Department of Livestock Services, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. My work combines clinical veterinary practice with public-sector livestock development — from treating sick cattle at the upazila veterinary hospital to leading vaccination campaigns, breed improvement programs and farmer training across the upazila.

I believe healthy animals build healthy livelihoods. Every day, my team and I work to bring modern, science-based animal healthcare to the doorsteps of smallholder farmers.

Read My Full Story

item.title: About
item.dc:creator: drmajumder
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Manobendro Majumder, DVM

Upazila Livestock Officer, Baliakandi, Rajbari
Department of Livestock Services, Government of Bangladesh

I grew up in rural Bangladesh, where I saw first-hand how much a family's wellbeing depends on the health of its cattle, goats and poultry. That experience inspired me to become a veterinarian — and later, to dedicate my career to public veterinary service.

As Upazila Livestock Officer, I lead the government's livestock services in Baliakandi upazila: running the upazila veterinary hospital, supervising field staff, coordinating vaccination and breed-improvement programs, and advising hundreds of farm families every month.

Education & Qualifications

Professional Experience

  • Upazila Livestock Officer, Baliakandi, Rajbari — Department of Livestock Services (2021 – present, sample). Leading veterinary and livestock extension services for the entire upazila.
  • Veterinary Surgeon, Upazila Livestock Office — Department of Livestock Services (2016 – 2021, sample). Clinical treatment, surgery and artificial insemination services.
  • Veterinary Field Practitioner — Private and NGO-supported practice (2012 – 2016, sample). On-farm treatment and farmer advisory in rural communities.

Key Achievements

  • Coordinated upazila-wide FMD and PPR vaccination campaigns reaching tens of thousands of animals each year.
  • Expanded artificial insemination coverage, improving dairy productivity for smallholder farmers.
  • Trained hundreds of farmers and youth entrepreneurs in modern dairy, beef fattening and poultry management.
  • Strengthened disease surveillance and rapid-response reporting during avian influenza and lumpy skin disease alerts.

Memberships

  • Registered Veterinary Practitioner, Bangladesh Veterinary Council (BVC)
  • Member, The Bangladesh Veterinary Association (BVA)

"Healthy animals build healthy livelihoods. My mission is to bring science-based animal healthcare to the doorstep of every farm family in Baliakandi."

— Dr. Manobendro Majumder

item.title: Services
item.dc:creator: drmajumder
item.content:encoded:
The Upazila Livestock Office, Baliakandi provides the following veterinary and livestock development services. Most government services are free of charge or offered at a nominal government-fixed fee.

Clinical Treatment of Livestock

Diagnosis and treatment of diseases of cattle, buffalo, goats and sheep — including digestive, respiratory, reproductive and parasitic conditions — at the veterinary hospital and through farm visits.

Poultry Health & Biosecurity

Vaccination scheduling, disease prevention and biosecurity audits for commercial layer, broiler and backyard poultry, plus duck and pigeon health services.

Vaccination Campaigns

Mass vaccination programs against foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), anthrax, black quarter, PPR, rabies, Newcastle disease, fowl cholera and duck plague.

Artificial Insemination & Breed Improvement

AI services using quality-certified semen, pregnancy diagnosis, infertility management and guidance on improved cattle and goat breeds.

Farmer Training & Advisory

Training sessions and one-to-one advisory on dairy management, beef fattening, goat rearing, fodder cultivation, feed formulation and farm record keeping.

Disease Surveillance & Reporting

Continuous monitoring of livestock and zoonotic diseases, outbreak investigation, sample collection for laboratory diagnosis and coordination with district and national authorities.

Emergency cases

For after-hours emergencies (difficult calving, bloat, suspected anthrax or rabies exposure), contact the Upazila Livestock Office hotline immediately. Replace this text with the official hotline number.

item.title: Foot-and-Mouth Disease: Prevention Tips for Cattle Farmers in Rajbari
item.dc:creator: drmajumder
item.content:encoded:
Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) remains one of the most economically damaging livestock diseases in Bangladesh. While it rarely kills adult cattle, it sharply reduces milk yield, draft power and body condition — losses that hit smallholder families hardest.

Know the signs

  • High fever followed by blisters on the tongue, gums, muzzle, teats and between the hooves
  • Excessive drooling and smacking of the lips
  • Lameness and reluctance to stand
  • Sudden drop in milk production

Five prevention steps every farmer can take

  1. Vaccinate on schedule. Bring your cattle to the free government vaccination campaigns announced by the Upazila Livestock Office.
  2. Quarantine new animals for at least two weeks before mixing them with your herd.
  3. Disinfect shoes, vehicles and equipment that move between farms and markets.
  4. Avoid shared grazing and communal watering points during an outbreak.
  5. Report suspected cases immediately to the Upazila Livestock Office so we can respond before the disease spreads.

If you suspect FMD in your herd, do not panic and do not sell the animal at market — call the Upazila Livestock Office, Baliakandi. Early reporting protects your neighbours' animals as well as your own.

item.title: Why Artificial Insemination Pays Off for Smallholder Dairy Farmers
item.dc:creator: drmajumder
item.content:encoded:
Many farmers in Baliakandi still rely on natural service with local bulls. Artificial insemination (AI) with quality-certified semen is safer, cheaper in the long run, and the fastest path to a more productive herd.

The benefits in plain terms

  • Better calves: crossbred heifers from proven sires can produce several times more milk than local cattle.
  • Disease control: AI eliminates the breeding-related spread of brucellosis and other infections.
  • No bull-keeping costs: feeding and housing a breeding bull is expensive and often dangerous.
  • Record keeping: every AI service is documented, which helps plan calving, drying-off and vaccination.

When to call the AI technician

Timing is everything. Watch for standing heat — the cow stands still when mounted by others. The best window for insemination is roughly 12 hours after the first signs of standing heat. Call the office as soon as you notice heat signs in the morning; we aim to provide same-day service.

AI services are available at the Upazila Livestock Office, Baliakandi at the government-fixed fee. Ask us about pregnancy diagnosis and follow-up care as well.
item.excerpt:encoded: Artificial insemination is safer and more profitable than keeping a bull. Here is what every smallholder dairy farmer should know about AI.

item.title: Preparing Your Poultry Flock for the Monsoon Season
item.dc:creator: drmajumder
item.content:encoded:
The monsoon brings welcome rain to our fields — and a wave of poultry health problems: coccidiosis, fowl cholera, Newcastle disease and fungal feed contamination all spike in the wet months. A little preparation now saves a lot of loss later.

A pre-monsoon checklist

  1. Repair the shed roof and raise the floor. A dry litter bed is your first line of defence against coccidiosis.
  2. Complete vaccinations before the rains. Make sure Newcastle disease and fowl cholera boosters are up to date.
  3. Store feed off the ground in sealed containers — damp feed grows toxic moulds within days.
  4. Improve ventilation while keeping rain out; humid, stagnant air spreads respiratory disease.
  5. Provide clean drinking water. Flood water carries pathogens — never let birds drink from puddles.

The Upazila Livestock Office runs free Newcastle disease vaccination drives for backyard poultry before every monsoon. Watch for announcements at your union parishad office, or contact us directly to register your village.
item.excerpt:encoded: Wet months mean coccidiosis, fowl cholera and mouldy feed. Use this pre-monsoon checklist to keep your flock healthy through the rains.
